detail.longDescription: When I clone a repository from a URL that redirects, Git follows the redirect but keeps the original URL as the origin remote. For example: $ git clone https://tangled.org/quokka.wiki/test-repo Cloning into 'test-repo'... warning: redirecting to https://knot.quokka.wiki/did:plc:zrbnjks5yw3rydtzhtdqgufv/ ... After cloning: $ git remote -v origin https://tangled.org/quokka.wiki/test-repo (fetch) origin https://tangled.org/quokka.wiki/test-repo (push) Is there a Git option or configuration setting that makes Git automatically update origin to the final URL when a clone follows an HTTP redirect? In this example, I'd like origin to automatically be set to: https://knot.quokka.wiki/did:plc:zrbnjks5yw3rydtzhtdqgufv/ rather than retaining the original https://tangled.org/quokka.wiki/test-repo URL?
